standard_prerequisites.name: Eilenberg-MacLane objects
standard_prerequisites.statement: The simplicial object K(A,k) with K(A,k)_n the direct sum of copies of A indexed by surjections [n] to [k], zero in degrees below k.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the middle term's two ends in the displayed sequence (source lines 3776-3777, 3789-3792).

standard_prerequisites.name: Simplicial objects defined by index sets
standard_prerequisites.statement: A simplicial object described by direct sums indexed by a set of maps out of [n], with structure maps induced by composition of indices.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the definition of E in the statement and what makes the maps simplicial (source lines 3778-3788, 3800-3801).

standard_prerequisites.name: Term by term split short exact sequences
standard_prerequisites.statement: A short exact sequence of simplicial objects which is split in every degree by the inclusions and projections of direct summands.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the conclusion of the statement (source line 3793).

core_obligations: Identify the maps: read the map K(A,k) to E as the inclusion of a direct summand and E to K(A,k+1) as the projection onto a direct summand, using the inclusion of index sets (source lines 3796-3799).
Check the structure: verify that both maps are morphisms of simplicial objects, which is immediate because the structure maps are induced by composition of indices (source lines 3799-3801).
Record the exactness: the composite is zero and the sequence is split in each degree by construction, giving the term-by-term split short exact sequence (statement, source lines 3789-3793).

proof_roadmap.step: Identify the two maps as the inclusion and projection of direct summands controlled by the index sets.
Observe they are morphisms of simplicial objects, which gives the term-by-term split short exact sequence.

difficulty_reason: The counted unit is the author's own lemma lemma-extension at source lines 3772-3794: for an object A of an abelian category and k at least 0, the simplicial object E whose n-simplices are the direct sum of copies of A indexed by the maps [n] to [k+1] with image [k] or [k+1] fits into a short exact sequence 0 to K(A,k) to E to K(A,k+1) to 0 which is term by term split. The proof at source lines 3796-3802 is a three-sentence construction check: the two maps are the inclusion and projection of the obvious direct summands, their composure properties are read off from the inclusions of index sets, and they are visibly morphisms of simplicial objects because the structure maps are induced by composition of indices. The card's substance is therefore the construction itself, which the statement spells out in full.
